extracted.intended_audience: public relations/public affairs/communications practitioners and agencies preparing submissions to the PRSA Anvil Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and judging criteria for entering PRSA's Anvil Awards, covering Silver (strategic campaign and organizational) and Bronze (tactical) categories, required materials, eligibility, and how entries will be evaluated. Intended for teams preparing award case studies, summaries, and supporting materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Silver Anvil Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Silver Anvil Awards celebrate the best strategic communications campaigns of the year, as well as outstanding organizational excellence. They must meet the highest standards of performance in the profession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Bronze Anvil Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Bronze Anvil Awards recognize outstanding communications tactics that contribute to the success of overall programs or campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging: one winner and up to two runners-up per category
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges will select only one Anvil, and up to two runners-up in each category/subcategory. In categories for which judges determine there is no winner (entries do not merit award), there will be no runner-up awards given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline: finalist and winner notification
rubrics_metrics.description: Finalists in each category will be notified by the end of March 2024, and winners will be announced in May 2024 at the Anvil Awards Ceremony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Community Relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs that aim to improve relations with, or seek to win the support or cooperation of, people or organizations in communities in which the sponsoring organization has an interest, need or opportunity. 'Community' in this category refers to a specific geographic location or locations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Content Marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs that effectively demonstrate a strategic program that includes creating and distributing valuable content to attract, acquire, and engage target audience(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examples and metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Crisis Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs undertaken to deal with an unplanned event that required an immediate response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Events and Observances
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes virtual or in-person programs or events, such as commemorations, observances, conferences, openings, yearlong anniversaries, celebrations or other special activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Events longer than one week enter in 'More Than Seven Days'; events within one week enter in 'Seven Or Fewer Days'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Financial Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs directed to shareholders, other investors and the investment community; includes communication programs related to decentralized currencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Global Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes any type of program, such as Reputation/Brand Management, Marketing or Events and Observances, that demonstrates effective global communications implemented in more than one country.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Influencer Marketing (macro/micro)
rubrics_metrics.description: Distinguishes macro-influencers (celebrities, executives, bloggers, journalists with 10,000–1M followers) and micro-influencers (everyday consumers/employees/industry experts with 500–10,000 followers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Macro-influencers: high topical relevance; Micro-influencers: high brand relevance/resonance driven by personal experience and relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Integrated Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes creative and effective integrated campaigns, along with other marketing or communications including paid, earned, shared and owned efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate meaningful PR/communications components and how they integrated with other disciplines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Internal Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs targeted specifically to special publics directly allied with an organization, such as employees, members, affiliated dealers and franchisees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Issues Management
rubrics_metrics.description: For programs undertaken to deal with issues that could extraordinarily affect ongoing business strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Marketing
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs designed to introduce new products/services or promote existing products/services to a particular audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories for B2B, consumer products (regional vs national/international), consumer services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Most Effective Campaign on a $5,000 to $10,000 Budget
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective campaign delivered within parameters of a limited budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not include staff time and overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Most Effective Campaign on a Shoestring Budget ($5,000 or less)
rubrics_metrics.description: Successful campaign despite constraints of a small budget.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This does not include staff time and overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Most Effective DEI Campaign
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts devoted to promoting inclusivity and/or dismantle discrimination for racial, ethnic, religious or sexual orientation and gender differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Climate Action & Environmental Sustainability
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors excellence in energy efficiency, natural resources, programs and campaigns that limit greenhouse gas emissions, minimize waste and contamination, protect and restore ecosystems, and contribute to the adaptation to climate change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Corporate Citizenship
rubrics_metrics.description: Celebrates campaigns and programs that ignite individuals, technology, and partnerships to create positive impact for society at the local, national or international level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes areas such as poverty, hunger, housing, health and well-being, climate, equity, education, and human rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Multicultural Public Relations
rubrics_metrics.description: For any type of program specifically targeted to a cultural group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Public Affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs specifically designed to influence public policy and/or affect legislation, regulations, political activities or candidacies at local, state or federal levels so that the entity funding the program benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Public Service
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes programs that advance public understanding of societal issues, problems or concerns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subcategories for Associations/Government/Nonprofit, Business, and Partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Reputation/Brand Management
rubrics_metrics.description: Programs designed to enhance, promote or improve the reputation of an organization with its publics or key elements of its publics, either proactively or in response to an issue, event or market occurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best of Silver Anvil selection
rubrics_metrics.description: A Best of Silver Anvil Award recipient is selected from among the year’s Silver Anvil Strategic Campaign Award winners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Represents the pinnacle of excellence in public relations programming and demonstrates PR strategic value and ability to drive critical business outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Anvil four judging criteria (insights and analysis, planning, execution, evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Anvil Judges will evaluate your entry on the merit of the four criteria — insights and analysis, planning, execution and evaluation — that you share in your two-page summary and supporting materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your entry should begin with a brief situation analysis for your program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Two-Page Summary requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The two-page summary (to be uploaded as a PDF) is the single-most important component of a Silver Anvil Strategic Campaign entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It should begin with a brief situation analysis for your program, followed by addressing each of the four entry criteria — insights and analysis, planning, execution, and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Supporting Materials upload rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants will be instructed to upload four separate PDFs (no more than 225 pages each with a maximum file size of 10MB) of any detailed supporting materials referenced in the insights and analysis, planning, execution and evaluation sections of your two-page summary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The absence of relevant and meaningful supporting materials will result in significantly lower scores, effectively eliminating the entry from consideration. Uploaded documents must be PDFs; pages no larger than 8.5 x 11 inches (A4 for international entries) with a minimum 10-point typeface and one-inch margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insights and Analysis (detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: What methods/strategies/tools were implemented to arrive at your insights into and analysis of the campaign?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State what type of research was used — primary, secondary or both. Primary research includes focus groups, interviews, data and analytics, surveys. Secondary research includes online database searches, web research, library searches, industry reports, internal market analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning (detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: How did the plan correlate to the insights gathered at the end of the campaign? What was the plan in general terms?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include specific, measurable objectives; target audiences; overall strategy; and budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution (detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: How was the plan executed, and what was the outcome?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe activity flow, key tactics, difficulties encountered and how handled, other organizations involved, and whether nontraditional PR tactics (e.g., advertising) were used. Note: unless entering under Integrated Communications, advertising costs should not exceed one-third of the budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation (detail)
rubrics_metrics.description: What methods of evaluation were used and what were your results?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare results to the specific, measurable objectives identified in planning and explain how well results reflect original strategy and planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Organizational Award: Best In-House Team submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary: overview of the business/organization and detailed description of outstanding accomplishments/strategic benchmarks within the award program timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate the role of the in-house team from any externally employed resources; include examples of measurable impact, challenges handled, creative/innovative programs, influence on behavioral/attitudinal change, fostering positive working culture. Case study upload: two brief case studies (each 500 words or fewer) or current Silver Anvil submissions. Provide number of employees on the team and annual public relations budget (including staffing costs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Organizational Award: Best Agency submission requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary: overview of the agency, offerings, and detailed description of outstanding accomplishments/strategic benchmarks within award timeframe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include measurable impact for clients, challenges handled, creative programs, influence on behavior/attitudes, and company culture. Case studies: two brief case studies (each 500 words or fewer) or current Silver submissions. Provide number of employees, annual revenue, and a client list from the past 12 months (uploaded as one-page PDF) including tenure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Organizational Award: Best Solution Provider/Vendor
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary: overview of the company and services provided and how services are first in class and tailored to support the communication industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit two letters of recommendation from customers/clients in support of the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Organizational Award: Organization With the Most Impactful DEI Program
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary: overview of the team leading DEI efforts and detailed description of programs, practices and initiatives instituted to bring about positive DEI change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examples of new resources for diverse employees/customers (language translations, sharing forums), internal programming, how efforts advance DEI outside their organization, and future plans. Case studies: two brief case studies (each 500 words or fewer) or current Silver submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Organizational Award: Best College/University Communications Program/Department
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary: overview of the educational institution and description of outstanding accomplishments within the last 12 months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include examples of student job readiness, metrics such as admissions, graduation trends, first-year employment, internship placement, academic achievements, and other measurable results. Requirements: the institution must have a PRSSA chapter and hold a Certificate in Education for Academic Programs in Public Relations (CEPR). Provide number of educators (full-time, part-time, adjunct) and faculty PRSA involvement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Organizational Award: Best AI Integration and Digital Innovations
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary: overview of the organization and detailed descriptions of exceptional creativity, effectiveness, and ingenuity in leveraging digital innovations, particularly AI, to revolutionize PR/comms strategies and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of successful implementation of AI-driven technologies that enhanced visibility, engagement, efficiencies and overall PR performance. Case studies: two brief case studies (each 500 words or fewer) or current Anvil submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Silver Organizational Award: Oak Award requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary: historical overview of the organization and detailed description of outstanding accomplishments/strategic benchmarks achieved over their history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries must show sustained growth and overall impact on the industry. Provide list of accomplishments and awards and list of prominent leaders and their accomplishments (including those who contributed to future success).

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze One-Page Summary requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise summary no longer than one page must be uploaded as a PDF. The one-page summary is the single most important component of a Bronze Anvil Tactical Award entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Judging Criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Anvil Judges evaluate Bronze entries on four key areas — planning/content, creativity/quality, technical excellence and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media relations categories are not judged on technical excellence. The summary should include measurable objectives, target audiences, budget and other specific information requested in the individual category. Results (qualitative or quantitative) should provide evidence of how objectives were met and how the entry impacted a broader or ongoing program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Paid Promotions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of sponsorships, paid placements, or other marketing communications tactics that complement a broader public relations strategy or approach and generate exceptional ROI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts should be targeted and strategic and demonstrate a distinct purpose that aligns with goals of an overarching campaign or specific desired outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Media Relations
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactics, programs and events driven entirely by media relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit press releases, media advisories, pitch letters, requests for coverage, etc., along with the one-page summary that includes measurable objectives and results, including media impact. Upload or provide YouTube/Vimeo links to any television or radio coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Feature Stories
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature articles that have been written by a practitioner and submitted and published through his/her efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit text of feature article and documentation of publication/placement. One-page summary should include target audience, measurable objectives and documented results. Articles must be written in their entirety or substantively by the entrant, and not merely 'pitched.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Executive Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Positioning of an executive at any level across earned, owned, and shared platforms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-page summary should include information about the executive and stated objectives, quantification of results and copies of significant placements, social media posts or memos.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Social Media
rubrics_metrics.description: How did you use social media to tell a story or connect with an audience?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share screenshots or links to work and provide detailed results focusing on engagement and conversions. Subcategories: Single Channel Use, Multichannel Use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Influencer Marketing (tactical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tactic that focuses on using paid spokespeople and key leaders to increase awareness and drive your brand's message to the larger market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include details of achievements/benchmarks on how the spokesperson met/exceeded campaign goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Best Use of AI
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate how AI played a pivotal role in successfully driving or enhancing traditional tactical efforts within a campaign.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of tools used and results from their use. Subcategories include Direct Audience Engagement, Media Relations, Social Media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Digital Platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Did you launch or substantially enhance a digital platform?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how it was launched, amount of risk in marketing plan, what value the end user received and how it matched goals. Include metrics and benchmarks. Entry can be completed by a vendor or the customer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Data Insights
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of data or research in a program to inform a communications strategy and/or message development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate how the insights were acquired and applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Websites
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a website as part of a communications or content marketing program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include screen grabs or copies of key pages to support the one-page summary, include the website URL for external sites and how the site met or exceeded communications benchmarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Non-Traditional Tactics
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovative, unconventional, creative tactics or approaches used as part of a PR program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include documentation of how the tactic specifically contributed to measurable results; photographic/video representation of any physical objects should be uploaded to be fully considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Annual Reports
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications that report on an organization’s annual performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload a sample of one copy along with a one-page summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Blogs/Vlogs
rubrics_metrics.description: Web-based journals, or blogs, that communicated to a target audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-page summary should include rationale for blogging strategy, target audiences and statistics or other quantifiable measurement to support objectives. Submit screen downloads and the site URL.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Newsletters
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications – digital or print – designed, written and published/distributed periodically to provide brief and timely information to target audiences while supporting overall objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload samples of three consecutive issues, along with a one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Single-Issue Publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Single-issue publications designed for a special purpose; books and other publications not eligible in other categories enter here.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload a sample of one copy along with the one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Magazines
rubrics_metrics.description: Publications designed to provide in-depth information about an organization or topic on a regular basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload samples of three consecutive issues along with the one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Video
rubrics_metrics.description: Produced videos to inform target audiences of an event, brand, product, service, issue or organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One-page summary should include usage statistics or other quantified measurement to support stated objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Branded Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of content generation to promote a particular brand which funds the content's production.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload samples along with the one-page summary including goals and results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze Tactical Category: Podcasts
rubrics_metrics.description: How did you tell your story – was the purpose to teach or share? Was it intended for internal or external audiences and was there engagement on multiple platforms?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide goals, results and listener feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility time window
rubrics_metrics.description: At least some part of the work must have occurred during the period Feb 1, 2022 – Feb 1, 2024, though the program must have been initiated no earlier than Jan 1, 2022.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple categories policy
rubrics_metrics.description: An entry may be submitted in multiple categories, provided it applies to the specific criteria stated within each category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants should use the 'Copy Submission' link to duplicate an entry. Judges will not move entries to better suited categories; entrants should examine program objectives and target audiences when choosing categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic entry information fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants must select category being entered, title of the entry (each title must be unique), name of the organization/client, name of the agency (if any) and a 100-word description of the program/submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image submission specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Upload up to three graphic images representative of your program. Images will be featured onscreen during the ceremony and may be featured in PRSA publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable file formats: jpg, tif, eps, native Illustrator, Photoshop or hi-res pdf files. Artwork should be at least 1,000 pixels or more in either width or height.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries produced in a language other than English must be translated prior to submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics compliance requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: By entering the Anvil Awards, all entrants confirm that their programs and entries comply with the ethical standards of the profession, as embodied in the PRSA Code of Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an entry has an aspect of 'ethics performance' that is instructive and vital to the program, include commentary of no more than four sentences. PRSA may take action if aware of non-compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: File formatting rules for uploaded documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Uploaded documents must be uploaded as PDFs. Pages should be no larger than 8.5 x 11 inches (A4 for international entries) with a minimum of 10-point typeface and one-inch margins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advertising budget cap outside Integrated Communications
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless you are entering this program under 'Integrated Communications,' advertising costs should not exceed one-third of the budget.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bronze supporting materials and media types
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants will be asked to upload supporting documents and back-up materials as requested in each individual category, e.g., PDFs, videos, audio, video links, website URLs, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Media relations categories scoring exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Media relations categories are not judged on technical excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Most Effective on Budget categories: budget definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For categories honoring most effective campaigns within specific budget ranges, the budget referenced does not include staff time and overhead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature story authorship requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Feature articles submitted must be written in their entirety or substantively by the entrant and not merely pitched.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entries become property and judges' decisions final
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries become the property of PRSA. The decisions of the judges are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines and fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry deadlines and fees vary by entry type and membership status (PRSA member vs non-member) and by deadline stage (early, regular, final).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the official fees table for specific category pricing and deadline dates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best Solution Provider/Vendor: required substantiation
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary describing how services are first in class and tailored to support the communication industry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include two letters of recommendation from customers/clients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best AI Integration and Digital Innovations: submission details
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary describing exceptional creativity and results using digital innovations, particularly AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide examples of AI-driven technologies implementation and case studies (two brief case studies, each 500 words or fewer).

rubrics_metrics.name: Oak Award: evidence of longevity and impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary and supporting materials must show sustained growth and overall impact on the industry over the organization's history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide accomplishments and awards list and prominent leaders and their accomplishments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization With the Most Impactful DEI Program: evidence and future plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Two-page summary should describe programs/practices/initiatives that brought about positive DEI change and future plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include case studies and examples of resources, internal programming, and how efforts advance DEI externally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best College/University program: documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide metrics related to admissions, graduation, employment, internship placement, academic achievements and other measurable results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institution must have PRSSA chapter and CEPR certificate; include faculty counts and PRSA involvement.
